brief_cols.label: Who Meridian Is
brief_cols.text: Integrated health system and health plan operating Epic as core EHR, with a fragmented on-prem analytics estate (SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, SAS) and an outsourced analytics managed services provider consuming ~80% of delivery capacity on maintenance.

brief_cols.label: Where They Want to Go
brief_cols.text: Seven enterprise use cases are in scope: unified clinical + claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, and automated close. AWS and Databricks are the target platform direction — not yet production-ready.

brief_cols.label: What Is Blocking Progress
brief_cols.text: No certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no AI audit trail evidence. Provider contract terms are not digitized in governed form. All seven use cases require evidence closure before value can be quantified.

brief_cols.label: What Nexus Can Do Now
brief_cols.text: Nexus has mapped the enterprise context across 19 dimensions and 146 evidence references. It can surface use case hypotheses, identify gap-to-decision chains, and prioritize evidence collection. It cannot yet produce decision-grade sourcing outputs or quantified value claims.

priorities.title: Close the lakehouse foundation evidence gap
priorities.detail: Epic Clarity, Claims, and Pharmacy data harmonization must be certified before the unified clinical + claims lakehouse use case can advance. AWS/Databricks medallion architecture is aspirational — not yet evidenced.

priorities.title: Establish formal data governance and semantic layer
priorities.detail: No certified semantic layer and no formal governance operating model exist. This blocks all seven use cases, particularly AI/LLM automation, where audit trail and data quality rule evidence are also absent.

priorities.title: Digitize provider contract terms and certify attribution
priorities.detail: Provider contract terms are not in governed digital form. Attribution ownership is unproven. Both gaps block cost transparency and provider quality use cases from reaching decision grade.

priorities.title: Govern contact center transcripts and certify intent taxonomy
priorities.detail: Transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, and member identity linkage are all unproven. Call center optimization cannot advance to agent-assist or next-best-action without these foundations.

priorities.title: Certify payment integrity model lineage and recovery workflows
priorities.detail: SAS-based payment integrity models lack governed lineage. Provider entity resolution is unproven. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not yet evidenced, preventing leakage quantification.

signals.quote: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse is promising, but strategy is not decision-grade until Epic Clarity evidence closes — no certified medallion architecture.
Governed data foundation for AI/LLM automation is promising, but not decision-grade until Epic Clarity evidence closes — no formal data governance.
Call center optimization is promising, but not decision-grade until contact center transcript evidence closes — transcript governance not yet evidenced.
End-to-end cost transparency is promising, but not decision-grade until Claims administration platform evidence closes — provider contract terms not digitized in governed form.

evidence_gaps.summary: All seven Meridian use cases are blocked from decision-grade status by at least four evidence gaps each. The most pervasive blockers are: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no patient/member identity spine. These four gaps affect every use case and must be resolved before Nexus can produce sourcing-event outputs or quantified value claims.

gaps.title: No certified medallion architecture (AWS/Databricks)
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse cannot advance. No bronze/silver/gold data products are evidenced. Target state is aspirational only.

gaps.title: No formal data governance operating model
gaps.blocks: AI/LLM automation use case is not decision-grade. Blocks semantic layer certification, AI audit trail, and data quality rule enforcement across all use cases.

gaps.title: No certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: AI/LLM, cost transparency, and automated close use cases cannot produce governed outputs. SQL Server mart sprawl creates duplicated, ungoverned business rules.

gaps.title: No patient/member identity spine loaded
gaps.blocks: Unified lakehouse and call center optimization both require a resolved member identity. Claims, pharmacy, and EMR data cannot be joined without it.

gaps.title: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases cannot produce margin or attribution outputs. Capitation and value-based contract logic remain in manual documents.

gaps.title: Transcript governance and intent taxonomy not certified
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization cannot advance to agent assist or next-best-action. Real-time CRM integration and member identity linkage are also unproven.

gaps.title: Rules and model lineage not governed; provider entity resolution unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction cannot quantify recoveries. SAS model lineage is ungoverned. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not evidenced.

gaps.title: Close workflow integration unproven; finance semantic layer not evidenced
gaps.blocks: Automated close and reporting use case cannot advance. Manual reporting maintenance load and ungoverned metric definitions prevent close-cycle acceleration.

use_cases.summary: Nexus has identified seven enterprise use cases for Meridian Health System, each with a defined value hypothesis, system dependency chain, and evidence gap set. All seven are in planning/context stage. None are decision-grade. Value quantification requires baseline owner sign-off and evidence closure for each use case.

top_5.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
top_5.fn: Enterprise Data and Analytics / Clinical Operations / Health Plan Operations
top_5.value: Governed longitudinal patient/member view enabling population health, cost, and quality analytics. Value quantifiable only after EMR, claims, pharmacy, identity, medallion, and governance evidence are certified.
top_5.gate: Epic Clarity medallion architecture + patient identity spine + claims/pharmacy harmonization + AWS/Databricks foundation
top_5.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CMO, and CDAO all cite this as the foundational strategic priority. It is the prerequisite platform for four of the other six use cases.

top_5.name: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM Automation
top_5.fn: Enterprise Data and Analytics / Health Plan Operations / Finance and Actuarial
top_5.value: Enables prior-auth, coding, and utilization management automation. Value quantifiable only after governance, semantic ownership, lineage, and control evidence are in place and workflow baselines are captured.
top_5.gate: Formal data governance operating model + certified semantic layer + AI audit trail + data quality rules
top_5.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, Health Plan Ops, and Procurement all flag this as a top priority. It is the governance prerequisite for all AI/LLM use cases.

top_5.name: Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction
top_5.fn: Health Plan Operations / Finance and Actuarial / Analytics
top_5.value: Reduces claims leakage through anomaly detection, FWA identification, and billing pattern analysis. Value quantifiable only after claims anomaly features, provider resolution, rules lineage, and recovery workflow evidence are governed.
top_5.gate: SAS model lineage governance + provider entity resolution + investigation workflow evidence + recovery tracking
top_5.why_this_is_top_5: CFO and Chief Experience Officer both flag payment integrity as a top strategic priority. SAS estate is the current detection platform but lacks governed lineage.

top_5.name: End-to-End Cost Transparency
top_5.fn: Finance and Actuarial / Health Plan Operations / Network Contracting
top_5.value: Creates cost-of-care and margin visibility across claims, capitation, and provider contracts. Value quantifiable only after claims, capitation, contract, and GL reconciliation evidence is governed and finance/actuarial baseline is signed off.
top_5.gate: Provider contract digitization + claims/GL calendar alignment + cost allocation rules + margin semantic model
top_5.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, and CDAO all cite cost transparency as a top priority. Provider contract terms not being in governed digital form is the single largest blocker.

top_5.name: Call Center Optimization
top_5.fn: Contact Center and Member Experience / Health Plan Operations
top_5.value: Improves agent assist and next-best-action using transcripts, CRM cases, and claims status. Value quantifiable only after transcript, CRM, claims, intent, and QA-label evidence is governed and baseline AHT/containment/FCR data are loaded.
top_5.gate: Transcript governance + real-time CRM integration + intent taxonomy certification + member identity linkage
top_5.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, and CIO all flag call center optimization. Chief Experience Officer owns member experience outcomes. Contact center platform and CRM are current-core but ungoverned for analytics.

use_cases.portfolio_view: All 7 use cases are in planning stage. The lakehouse and AI/LLM governance use cases are foundational prerequisites for the remaining five. Sequencing recommendation: close lakehouse and governance evidence first, then advance cost transparency and payment integrity in parallel, then call center and provider quality, then automated close.

quality_assessment.story_strength: The enterprise story is coherent and well-bounded: Meridian is an integrated payer-provider with a strong Epic clinical core, a fragmented on-prem analytics estate, and seven high-priority use cases that are all blocked by the same four foundational gaps (medallion architecture, data governance, semantic layer, identity spine). The narrative is honest about what Nexus can and cannot support, and the evidence gap structure gives executives a clear action agenda. The story would reach full McKinsey bar if baseline metrics (AHT, close cycle days, leakage rate) were loaded and value hypotheses could be bounded with directional ranges.
known_weaknesses: No baseline metrics loaded for any use case — AHT, close cycle, leakage rate, and HEDIS/STAR scores are all absent, preventing even directional value ranging.
Commercial contract terms are not evidenced for any vendor — total IT spend, vendor concentration risk, and renewal exposure cannot be assessed.
AWS and Databricks platform readiness is aspirational only — no network, security, IAM, or medallion architecture evidence exists, making the lakehouse timeline unassessable.
Finance and Actuarial function is candidate-status only — cost transparency and automated close use cases lack a confirmed finance owner.
Provider contract terms are in manual documents — digitization scope and timeline are unknown, blocking two use cases from advancing.
Workforce roles dimension has zero active rows — all 216 rows are candidate, meaning role-level accountability for evidence closure cannot be assigned.
quality_assessment.why_this_is_better_than_current: The current state at Meridian is a fragmented analytics estate with duplicated business rules, an outsourced managed services provider consuming ~80% of capacity on maintenance, and no shared governance model. Nexus provides the first integrated view of all 19 enterprise dimensions, maps the 24 specific evidence gaps blocking the 7 use cases, and gives the executive team a structured evidence closure agenda — replacing ad hoc stakeholder interviews with a governed, traceable context layer.
